clue.text: One following another win I have

parts.note: a win is a success
I have contracts to I've

explanation.surface: Someone boasts of a win, one coming after another.
explanation.definitionFit: Successive things come in an unbroken sequence, each after the last.

clue.text: Troubled courts holding record for one creating figures

indicators.note: holding means the rearranged letters go around the record's letters
troubled means disturbed, so the letters of courts are shaken into a new order

parts.note: LP is a long-playing record

explanation.surface: Law courts in turmoil hold a record for an artist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Troubled' signals the anagram and 'holding' the container; 'figures' suggests numbers, but here means statues.
explanation.definitionFit: A sculptor carves or models statues and other three-dimensional forms.

clue.text: Initially coax United States to overcome mismanaged trade

indicators.note: initially means the opening letter of each of the following words is taken

explanation.surface: Advice to coax America into fixing its badly handled commerce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Initially' applies to all six words that follow, not just 'coax'; reading 'United States' as US is a false trail.
explanation.definitionFit: Custom means a shop's business from its regular patrons, its trade.

clue.text: Rubber retreads we try from time to time

indicators.note: from time to time means only every other letter of the words retreads we try is used

explanation.surface: We try out remoulded tyres now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from time to time' takes the 2nd, 4th, 6th letters and so on of RETREADSWETRY.
explanation.definitionFit: In British English a rubber is a pencil eraser.

clue.text: Support for paramedics?

parts.note: seemingly backing for ambulance staff, but the support is the carrying frame they use

explanation.surface: Asking how to back up ambulance crews.
explanation.definitionFit: Paramedics carry patients on a frame that supports the casualty's body.

clue.text: Number in rowing team on Severn occasionally

parts.note: an eight is a rowing crew of eight oarsmen

indicators.note: occasionally means only some, alternate, letters of the word Severn are taken

explanation.surface: A rowing crew out on the River Severn now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occasionally' takes EEN, the 2nd, 4th and 6th letters of SEVERN, Britain's longest river.
explanation.definitionFit: Eighteen is a number, ten plus eight.

clue.text: Dad intermittently uses way through mountains

parts.note: Pa is an informal word for father

indicators.note: intermittently means only every other letter of the word uses is kept

explanation.surface: A father now and then takes a mountain route.
explanation.walkthrough: 'intermittently' keeps the 2nd and 4th letters of USES, giving SS.
explanation.definitionFit: A pass is a gap or route that crosses a mountain range.

clue.text: Type of bars, standard with all the Spanish

parts.note: par is the standard or norm
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: Bars of a standard type, together with all the Spanish ones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bars' looks like pubs; these are gymnastics apparatus.
explanation.definitionFit: Parallel bars are a gymnastic apparatus of two raised rails side by side.

clue.text: Taking sides, asked the French to note essential framework

indicators.note: taking sides means removing the outer letters, the sides, of asked

parts.note: le is French for the

explanation.surface: Siding with someone, a French person was asked to notice the basic structure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking sides' strips ASKED to SKE; it looks like picking a side in an argument.
explanation.definitionFit: A skeleton is the bare outline or structure of something, like a body's bones.

clue.text: Curious as purist finds a higher level

indicators.note: curious suggests something odd, so the letters of as purist are arranged oddly

explanation.surface: A strict purist, oddly, rises to a loftier plane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Curious' is the anagram signal for AS PURIST.
explanation.definitionFit: The upper floor of a house is a higher storey than the ground floor.

clue.text: Study after tabloid backed plot

indicators.note: after puts the study's word behind the tabloid's
backed means the word for the tabloid is written backwards

parts.note: a rag is a disparaging word for a tabloid newspaper
a den is a private study room

explanation.surface: Research follows a tabloid's support for a scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' reverses the tabloid word and 'after' places the study behind it. 'plot' looks like a scheme but is a patch of ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A plot of land planted with flowers or vegetables is a typical garden.

clue.text: Strict limits of territory in land one owns

parts.note: proper, in its strict sense, means exact or correct

indicators.note: limits of picks out the outermost letters of the word territory

explanation.surface: Firm borders mark out a territory within an estate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'limits of' gives T and Y, the end letters of TERRITORY.
explanation.definitionFit: Property means real estate: fields, buildings or plots belonging to someone.

clue.text: One accepting offer involving Liberal speaker

indicators.note: involving means the word for the one accepting goes around the Liberal letter

parts.note: someone who takes up an offer is a taker

explanation.surface: A person taking up a deal from a Liberal politician who makes speeches.
explanation.definitionFit: Anyone who speaks, especially a lot, is a talker.

clue.text: Conceal skin

definitions.meaning: an animal's pelt, as tanned into leather

explanation.surface: Hide your skin.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means keep secret; the noun is an animal pelt, two unrelated senses.

clue.text: Ed sent up style of writing with negative effect for subordinate

indicators.note: sent up means the name is written upward, reversed, in this down clue

parts.note: Ed is a name, taken letter for letter
a writer's pen is their style of writing
a dent is a setback or negative effect, as on finances

explanation.surface: Ed was mocked for a writing style that had a bad effect on a junior.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent up' looks like mocked but reverses ED to DE.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who relies on or is under another person is reliant and lower in rank.

clue.text: Fugitive on exposed jeep skirting smoky air

indicators.note: skirting means running along the edge, so the jeep's letters sit beside the smoky air word

parts.note: re means on or concerning
fug is a stuffy, smoky atmosphere

indicators.note: exposed means stripped of its outer covering, so the jeep loses its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A runaway on an open-topped jeep passes through hazy air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exposed' strips JEEP to EE; 'skirting' sets EE alongside FUG, at its end.
explanation.definitionFit: A refugee is someone who has fled, usually from war or persecution.

clue.text: All in quarantine — very onerous

indicators.note: in means the letters sit within the words quarantine very onerous

explanation.surface: Everybody is in isolation, and it is very burdensome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' signals the run of letters across QUARANTINE VERY ONEROUS.
explanation.definitionFit: All people taken together, every single person.

clue.text: Ma erupts in a frenzy going against the flow

indicators.note: in a frenzy suggests wild disorder, so the letters of Ma erupts are scrambled

explanation.surface: Mother explodes furiously, refusing to go along with things.
explanation.definitionFit: Upstream means towards a river's source, opposite to its current.

clue.text: Cultivated pair of journalists hugging posh moggie

indicators.note: hugging means the journalists' letters wrap around the posh and moggie pieces

parts.note: ed, short for editor, is a journalist; two give eded
U means upper class, posh
moggie is British slang for a cat

explanation.surface: Two refined journalists cuddle an upper-class cat.
explanation.walkthrough: A moggie is everyday British slang for an ordinary pet cat.
explanation.definitionFit: A cultivated person is refined and well schooled.

clue.text: Finally driving unfinished road in close country

indicators.note: in places the driving and road letters within the word for close

parts.note: the close of something is its end

indicators.note: finally picks the final letter of the word driving
unfinished means the road's word loses its last letter

parts.note: a lane is a narrow road

explanation.surface: At the end of a drive along a dead-end lane you reach the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finally' takes the last letter of driving, 'unfinished' drops the road's last letter, and 'in' sets both within the close. 'close' looks like near but is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: England is one of the nations making up the United Kingdom.

clue.text: Latterly, Romeo going for daughter in a proper fashion

indicators.note: going for means the Romeo letter is replaced by the daughter letter

parts.note: latterly means lately or recently
Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Recently, Romeo has courted a daughter respectably.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going for' looks like courting, but swaps R in RECENTLY for D.
explanation.definitionFit: Decently means respectably, in accordance with good standards.

clue.text: Wimp died; what's on their gravestone?

parts.note: d is the abbreviation for died, as in family trees
RIP, rest in peace, is the inscription on many gravestones

explanation.surface: A feeble person dies, and we wonder about the epitaph.
explanation.definitionFit: A drip is informal slang for a feeble, dull, spineless person.

clue.text: Highly motivated household finally torn apart

indicators.note: finally picks the closing letter of the word household

parts.note: riven means torn or split apart

explanation.surface: A determined family is ultimately split asunder.
explanation.definitionFit: A driven person is ambitious and relentlessly determined to succeed.

clue.text: Still holding second piece put in

indicators.note: holding means the motionless word contains the second's letter

parts.note: inert means motionless, still

explanation.surface: A motionless thing holds a second part inserted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' looks like an adverb, yet, but it is the adjective motionless.
explanation.definitionFit: An insert is an extra leaflet or section placed inside a publication.

clue.text: Lorry briefly going round cold northern region

indicators.note: going round means the lorry's word encircles the letter for cold

parts.note: artic is the short form of articulated lorry
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A truck makes a quick trip around a frozen northern area.
explanation.walkthrough: An artic is the British short name for an articulated lorry, a large truck with a separate cab.
explanation.definitionFit: The area around the North Pole is the polar region at the top of the globe.

clue.text: Coming onto the stage, fill with delight

definitions.meaning: an actor's appearance on stage, a noun
to enchant or captivate, a verb stressed on the second syllable

explanation.surface: An actor's arrival on stage thrills the audience.
explanation.definitionFit: Spelt alike but said differently: an actor's arrival on stage, and to captivate.

clue.text: Gathering around essentially historical group of trees

indicators.note: around means the gathering's word goes around the middle letters

parts.note: a fest is a festive gathering

indicators.note: essentially means the central letters at the heart of historical

explanation.surface: A festival held around a historic group of trees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'essentially' takes OR, the middle two of HISTORICAL's ten letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A forest is a large area thickly covered with trees.

clue.text: With great effort lifts about one ton — most weighty

indicators.note: about means the word for lifting goes round the one

parts.note: heaves means lifts with great effort
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A weightlifter strains to raise about a ton: the heaviest load.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts I inside HEAVES, giving HEAVIES, then T follows.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of heavy describes whatever has the greatest weight.

clue.text: Name of some winter months?

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Asking what a stretch of the winter months is called.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark hints that a period of winter months is also an academic or school session of the same name.
explanation.definitionFit: A term is a word or expression used to name something.

clue.text: Clearly record pocketing money in front of telly, oddly

indicators.note: in front of puts the record piece before the letters from the telly
pocketing means the record's word takes the money inside it

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record
tin is slang for money

indicators.note: oddly keeps the odd-numbered letters of the word telly

explanation.surface: A record stuffed with cash, seen oddly before the TV, is clearly strange.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' gives T, L, Y, the 1st, 3rd and 5th letters of TELLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Distinctly means in a way that is plain and easy to perceive.
